entries.title: CLI update: markdown-renderer

ai.title: Markdown fence detection rewritten as stateful line parser
ai.summary: The streaming markdown renderer in the CLI now tracks open code fences with a line-based state machine instead of counting backtick triplets. A new `LOOSE_FENCE_LINE` regex and `nextOpenFence` helper determine whether a fence is open, closed, or nonexistent, correctly handling indented lists, blockquotes, and the CommonMark rule that backtick runs with backticks in their info string do not open fences. `renderStreamingMarkdown` and `renderStreamingMarkdownIncremental` now call `openBacktickFenceIndex` to locate the pending fence, replacing previous `lastIndexOf` and even/odd count logic that misidentified mid-sentence ` ``` ` as fence boundaries.
ai.evidence: The diff replaces the naive `hasIncompleteCodeFence` implementation (which counted ` ``` ` occurrences modulo 2) with a line-by-line state machine using the new `LOOSE_FENCE_LINE` regex and `nextOpenFence` helper, and updates `renderStreamingMarkdown` and `renderStreamingMarkdownIncremental` to use `openBacktickFenceIndex` instead of `lastIndexOf`. New tests assert that fences nested in lists or blockquotes are correctly tracked and that backtick runs with info-string backticks do not open fences.

eli5.text: The assistant's text display now correctly identifies unfinished code blocks when they appear inside lists or quotes, or when they are just part of a sentence rather than actual code. This fixes a display glitch where the terminal would get confused about whether a block of text was code or regular writing. You will see answers with nested code examples or backticks in sentences render properly without breaking the layout. No action is needed from you, as this only improves how replies appear while they are being written.

ai.title: Context-aware key hint in Freebuff chat model picker
ai.summary: The Freebuff CLI chat model picker now displays a dynamic key hint instead of a fixed static string, computed by the new `freebuffChatPickerHint` function. The hint omits the arrow-key instruction when the catalog contains only a single model, preventing the misleading appearance of a keyboard bug on new accounts where arrows have no target row. It also omits the Tab key hint unless the currently focused model row exposes a reasoning effort ladder. The static hint previously rendered by `FreebuffChatControls` was removed because the selector component now has the state to determine which keys are actually active for the current context.
ai.evidence: In `cli/src/utils/freebuff-model-navigation.ts`, the new function `freebuffChatPickerHint` builds a key hint string that includes '↑↓ choose model' only when `params.modelCount > 1` and 'Tab reasoning' only when `params.focusedHasReasoning` is true. In `cli/src/components/freebuff-model-selector.tsx`, the scrollbox is extracted into a `list` constant; when `onSelectModel` is provided (the chat picker path), the component returns a box containing the dynamic hint above the list, replacing the previous static hint in `cli/src/components/freebuff-chat-controls.tsx`.

If you only have one model available, the hint stops mentioning the arrow keys, which previously made it look like the keys were broken. This makes the on-screen help accurate for both new accounts with a single model and existing users with many options.

testNames: unwraps a retry wrapped in data, and refuses a non-verdict

facts: GPT models sometimes send the scores as strings ("7") and the lists as JSON text. The output schema rejects them, and after its retries the judge ends with no output (every GPT-6 Luna verdict on 2026-10-30, GPT-6.1 Sol's on 2026-11-03). The verdict it meant is still in its last set_output call.
The judge's last set_output input, for recoverFromSetOutput.
entries.title: Evals update: judge

ai.title: BuffBench judge recovers verdicts from stringified output payloads
ai.summary: The BuffBench judging system in `evals/buffbench/judge.ts` now recovers verdicts from malformed structured outputs where GPT models send numeric scores as strings ("7") and lists as JSON text. The new `recoverFromSetOutput` function unwraps the last `set_output` tool call input, coerces string scores to numbers and parses JSON list strings, then validates the result against `JudgingResultSchema` before returning it. This fallback triggers when the structured output value is null or missing, a condition that caused every GPT-6 Luna verdict on 2026-10-30 and GPT-6.1 Sol's on 2026-11-03 to fail with no output.
ai.evidence: The diff adds `recoverFromSetOutput` to `evals/buffbench/judge.ts`, which coerces stringified scores and JSON text lists into valid types when `judgeResult.output.type !== 'structuredOutput'` or `judgeResult.output.value == null`.

eli5.text: The internal test system that scores AI coding work now rescues judgments from AI models when they submit scores in the wrong format, such as writing the number 7 as the word seven. This update only affects the Freebuff engineering team running their evaluations and does not change anything for regular users of the service. There is no visible effect on daily use or available features; it simply prevents valid scores from being lost due to formatting errors.
